The build is reproducible on this host across checkout directories: all 4 artifact sha256 values match dist/manifest.json. This is not a cross-machine reproducibility claim.
The artifact sizes and sha256 values in REPORT.md §9 and the manifest are accurate. Line count 2,780: confirmed.
The versions in REPORT §1 match go.mod, go.sum and the embedded build info: bubbletea v2.0.10, toml v1.6.0, go-winio v0.6.2, x/ansi v0.11.8, x/term v0.2.2, x/sys v0.46.0, go1.27.1.

The maintenance signals in REPORT §10 match the registry: ultraviolet is untagged (pinned 2026-07-03, latest 2026-10-01), cancelreader is from 2022, terminfo is pinned to 2022 while v1.2.0 exists, go-winio's last tag is 2024-04-09, and no bubbletea v3 exists.

Agent frame bounds hold on darwin and Linux. The probe sends exactly one 5-byte type-11 request and nothing else. The K1 replacement of control characters (C0, DEL, C1, invalid UTF-8) in key_type and comment is observed.

run passes stdin EOF and binary data (NUL, 0xFF) through. Large stderr while stdout goes unread does not deadlock, because stdio fds are passed raw with no copy goroutines. hard_gate_findings.evidence: (1) K3a contract violation, observed natively on Linux arm64: a reset after at least one response byte gives AGENT_UNAVAILABLE instead of AGENT_PROTOCOL_ERROR. The fix is small (frame.go ReadFrame: when n>0 or in the body read, wrap non-EOF read errors as protocol errors unless a deadline or cancel was hit). (2) Job-control defect in `run`: because the child's group is made the terminal foreground group, any other member of the same shell pipeline that reads the terminal is stopped with 'Stopped (tty input)'. Reproduced with macOS bash 3.2 and Linux busybox ash (4/4 variants on Linux). The contract is silent on pipelines, but this is a regression against plain exec. Everything else probed passed: stdin EOF, binary bytes, large stderr, grandchild, SIGPIPE, single delivery to the group, no orphan in 200 SIGTERM races, and all agent bounds.

code review only - not native evidence. The windows-x64 PE32+ builds and govulncheck/vet pass for GOOS=windows. Named pipe via go-winio DialPipeContext with context timeout; no server identity check. run_windows: no job object (a killed heimdall leaves the child), Ctrl-C is swallowed rather than forwarded, there is no CTRL_CLOSE/CTRL_BREAK handling, and .bat/.cmd quoting is unprotected (disclosed). Nothing was executed on Windows or WSL.

(a) Unbounded allocation from small untrusted input: the TOML parser (BurntSushi/toml v1.6.0 via profile.Parse) needs more than 2 GB for a 32 KB profile; profile show and tui are both exposed. (b) An undisclosed subprocess: the TUI runs `tmux` resolved from PATH when TMUX is set, with no timeout. (c) Environment variables change identity or behavior: DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES injects code into the darwin artifact (no hardened runtime; a release obligation that probably applies to every candidate), and GODEBUG=execerrdot=0 changes PATH resolution so a '.' entry runs. (d) There is no peer-credential check on the agent socket (disclosed). Verified positives: no shell use, no echo of secret values, agent lengths checked before allocation, no profile path TOCTOU, no runtime downloads, no sidecars.

Concerns: ultraviolet has no release tags (pinned pseudo-version 2026-07-03); cancelreader is from 2022; terminfo is pinned to a 2022 pseudo-version while v1.2.0 exists; go-winio's last tag is 2024-04-09. The TOML quadratic-memory behavior exists in the latest toml release.

Every linked module is MIT or BSD-3-Clause (license files checked). Go includes a PATENTS grant. Obligation: attribution notices must be shipped in binary distributions; they are not shipped now (disclosed). The prototype itself has no license (disclosed).

defects.description: `run` steals the terminal foreground from its own shell pipeline. With heimdall in a pipeline, a pipeline member that reads the tty (pagers, password prompts, interactive filters) gets SIGTTIN and the whole job shows 'Stopped (tty input)'. Reproduced on macOS bash (heimdall first in the pipeline) and on Linux busybox ash (all 4 variants); all controls without heimdall pass. The 50 ms watcher hands the terminal back to the child even after the shell runs `fg`.

Go runtime environment variables change security-relevant behavior. GODEBUG=execerrdot=0 makes `run` execute a command found through a '.' PATH entry (rc 0, against the default 127 refusal). GOTRACEBACK, GOMEMLIMIT and GOMAXPROCS are also honored. K7 allows either behavior, but the choice is controlled by the environment.

defects.description: Killing heimdall with SIGKILL, including killpg(SIGKILL) of its group, leaves the child running, because the child is always in its own process group (disclosed). The contract requires only that no orphan remains after a normal exit. The effect is that supervisors which kill heimdall's group (CI cancellation, timeout -s KILL) leak the child.

When heimdall is launched with fd 1 closed, the child does not inherit the closed descriptor: it gets a working fd 1 (the Go runtime reopens closed stdio at startup), so writes succeed (rc 0) where plain exec gives rc 1 'Bad file descriptor'. This is a small deviation from 'child inherits stdout'.
An unwritable --meta-file is detected only after the child has run. Heimdall exits with the child's code and reports the lost side channel only as one stderr line.

Bidi and zero-width code points (U+202E, U+200B) pass unchanged through agent comments, profile values, JSON and the TUI (Sanitize covers only C0/C1). This complies with K1/K2 but allows display spoofing in a security tool. Key names, not values, are echoed verbatim in key_path. A reviewer-crafted HEIMDALL_CANARY_ key name appeared in stdout and stderr, which the contract allows.

summary:
The harness verdict reproduces, but the hard gates do not all pass. My rebuild in /tmp/heimdall-review-go is byte-identical to the shipped artifacts (all 4 sha256 match the manifest). Re-running the shared harness against it gave 113/113, exit 0, verdict=pass on darwin-arm64, and the producer's selftest gave 59/59.

Probing beyond the harness found four major problems:
- **K3a contract violation on Linux.** A connection reset after one or more response bytes returns AGENT_UNAVAILABLE instead of AGENT_PROTOCOL_ERROR. Darwin delivers the reset as EOF, so the Darwin-only harness pass cannot detect it.
- **Profile parser memory blow-up.** Memory grows quadratically with TOML inline-table nesting inside [meta]. A 32 KB profile used more than 2 GB, and a 699 KB profile reached 26 GB RSS. The 1 MiB input bound does not bound parser resources.
- **`run` takes the terminal from its own pipeline.** Any other pipeline member that reads the tty is stopped with "Stopped (tty input)". This was seen with macOS bash and in every pipeline variant with Linux ash.
- **The TUI runs `tmux info` from PATH whenever TMUX is set, with no timeout.** A hung tmux blocks startup. REPORT does not disclose this.

Minor findings:
- DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES injects code into the unsigned darwin binary, and GODEBUG changes PATH resolution.
- A FIFO profile path hangs.
- SIGKILL leaves the child running (disclosed).
- A child launched with stdout closed gets a working fd 1.
- Several documentation inaccuracies.

Confirmed: the agent frame bounds, single-request passivity, byte-transparent stdio, no orphan in 200 SIGTERM races, distribution without a toolchain, licensing (notices still owed), dependency dates and versions, and CLI/TUI domain sharing.

Hard gates:
- Fail: child/IPC correctness and no unsupported security assumption.
- Pass: distribution, dependencies, licensing and domain sharing.
- Uncertain: Windows/WSL, which I could only review from code, not with native evidence.

All four major findings look fixable with small changes:
- wrap read errors after the first byte as protocol errors;
- add a nesting-depth or memory guard, or use another parser;
- do not take the foreground when stdin is not the session's job leader, or use a different signal model;
- pass tea.WithColorProfile or a filtered environment.

No escalation is needed for these defects. I wrote only under tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-go/review/. The exact PID I killed was my own runaway probe process.
